arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mach Mining's counsel argued Title VII prohibits suits without prior conciliation attempts.
The EEOC's counsel argued the Seventh Circuit correctly rejected broad judicial review.
Justice Kennedy noted the government's theory lacked strong case law support.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether federal courts can examine the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's pre-suit conciliation efforts. Mach Mining argues Title VII requires this modest inquiry. The EEOC contends the statute grants it exclusive discretion over settlement terms.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Mach Mining wants courts to verify the EEOC attempted good-faith conciliation.
The EEOC wants courts to defer entirely to its internal settlement decisions.

paragraphs: Mach Mining argues Title VII mandates a modest judicial inquiry into conciliation efforts.
The EEOC argues the statute grants it exclusive prerogative to define acceptable offers.

paragraphs: This case defines the scope of judicial oversight over federal agency enforcement. It determines whether private employers face unchecked administrative power. The outcome shapes the balance between agency discretion and statutory accountability.
